subject.title: fix: stop doctor misreporting trusted-proxy gateways as unauthenticated

question: Should Doctor accept runtime-authorizable, host-scoped trusted-proxy configuration as sufficient to replace the unauthenticated critical with a trusted-proxy exposure warning?
rationale: This is a deliberate security-diagnostic classification boundary: code review can establish that the helper is bounded and runtime-aligned, but maintainers must choose whether that warning level is the intended operator-security policy.

options.title: Approve the runtime-aligned diagnostic
options.body: Accept the reduced severity only for configurations that pass the new fail-closed readiness checks and preserve the existing exposure/firewall warning.

options.title: Keep the unauthenticated critical
options.body: Retain the existing token-oriented remediation for all exposed trusted-proxy configurations if maintainers do not want Doctor to model this auth boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve the runtime-aligned diagnostic
recommendation.body: Accept the reduced severity only for configurations that pass the new fail-closed readiness checks and preserve the existing exposure/firewall warning.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail shows repeated ownership of Gateway trusted-proxy security semantics and hardening.
